solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Television programme rock drummer missed or … (8,7)

indicatorNotes.rock: to rock is to shake, so the letters are shaken up

annotation.surface: A rock band's drummer failed to turn up, and the sentence trails off into the next clue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rock' sits beside 'drummer' as a music genre, but it is the verb. The ellipsis runs the sentence on into 9 across. Midsomer Murders is a long-running British TV detective series set in English villages.
annotation.definitionFit: Midsomer Murders is a British television detective drama, so it is a television programme.

entries.clue: Hebrew teacher inspires American hairstyling products (7)

indicatorNotes.inspires: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so MOSES takes US inside

blocks.note: Moses, the lawgiver who taught the Israelites

annotation.surface: A Hebrew teacher gives some American visitors the idea for hair products.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inspires' reads as giving an idea; it works in its literal Latin sense of breathing in.
annotation.definitionFit: Mousses are foams applied to hair to style and hold it.

entries.clue: Trick hollow mirrors removed from fairground amusement (5)

indicatorNotes.hollow: a hollow word keeps only its shell: MIRRORS becomes MS
indicatorNotes.removed from: those letters are taken away from DODGEMS

blocks.note: dodgems are the bumper cars at a fair
MIRRORS with its inside emptied, removed from DODGEMS

annotation.surface: Someone plays a trick by taking the mirrors out of a funfair's hall of mirrors.
annotation.walkthrough: The hall of mirrors is the fairground amusement the surface suggests, but the one needed is the dodgems, the bumper cars.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sly ruse for getting out of something, as in a tax dodge.

entries.clue: Leaves behind away team’s kit heading for stadium (9)

indicatorNotes.heading for: the head, or first letter, of STADIUM

blocks.note: away = out, as in 'she is out'
a team's strip is its playing kit

annotation.surface: The away team's kit arrives at the stadium ahead of the players.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Away team' looks like one football phrase, but the split falls between the two words. The 's belongs to the kit, not to a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To outstrip rivals is to leave them behind by going faster or further.

entries.clue: Rascal escapes imminent death (6)

indicatorNotes.escapes: IMP gets out of IMPENDING, leaving the rest

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal; it is the part removed

annotation.surface: A rascal narrowly escapes death.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a narrow escape; 'imminent death' looks like one phrase but 'imminent' is the fodder and 'death' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemism in reverse: death is the close of a life, and books and films speak of a character's end in the same way.

entries.clue: Batty woman arrived briefly upsetting centrepiece of musical medley (8)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, a word is cut short, so CAME loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.upsetting: in a down clue, upset turns NORA CAM upside down

blocks.note: Nora Batty, the wrinkled-stockinged character in the BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine

annotation.surface: A mad woman turns up and disrupts the middle of a musical medley.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Batty' reads as mad; it is the surname of Nora Batty, a famous British sitcom character from Last of the Summer Wine. Macaroni once meant a medley, hence macaronic verse.
annotation.definitionFit: Macaroni is an old word for a medley or jumble, the sense behind macaronic verse mixing languages.

entries.clue: Bank just ignores graduate (4)

indicatorNotes.ignores: to ignore something is to leave it out, so BARELY drops BA

blocks.note: just = barely, as in 'just made it'
a Bachelor of Arts, the part removed

annotation.surface: A bank only just turns down a graduate's application.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like the lender turning down a graduate; it is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym through the phrasal verb: you can bank on or count on a friend.

entries.clue: Cautioned when playing, gets coaching (9)

indicatorNotes.when playing: the letters of CAUTIONED are played about with

annotation.surface: A player booked during a match is sent off for extra coaching.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a footballer shown a yellow card; 'playing' is the signal to rearrange 'cautioned'.
annotation.definitionFit: Coaching is teaching or instruction, which is education.

entries.clue: Cunning minor takes drug (7)

indicatorNotes.takes: to take something is to take it in, so SLIGHT swallows the E

annotation.surface: A crafty youngster starts taking drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minor' reads as a child, suiting 'cunning'; it is the adjective meaning small.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: the word survives mainly in 'sleight of hand', a conjuror's crafty skill.

entries.clue: … saw by middle of June, day not specified (7)

indicatorNotes.middle of: takes the central letters of JUNE

blocks.note: the two central letters of JUNE
to see someone is to go out with them, so saw = dated

annotation.surface: Continuing 1 across: a drummer went missing, or was seen around mid-June on some unrecorded day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool or a proverb; here it is the past tense of seeing someone romantically. 'By' simply places the two pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a letter or document with no date written on it leaves its day unspecified.

entries.clue: University feeds craze concerning art, literature etc (7)

indicatorNotes.feeds: to feed something in is to insert it, so U goes into CULT RE

blocks.note: a cult is a fad or craze
re = concerning, as in memo headers

annotation.surface: A university fuels a fashionable craze for the arts.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition 'art, literature etc' sits at the end and describes the whole field rather than any single art.
annotation.definitionFit: Culture is the arts and intellectual achievement taken together.

entries.clue: Bribe corrupt Western Europeans being seized (9)

indicatorNotes.corrupt: the letters of WESTERN are corrupted into a new order
indicatorNotes.being seized: the two Es are taken into the mix

annotation.surface: A bribe offered to corrupt Western Europeans who are being arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective describing the Europeans, and 'bribe' supports that reading; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or bribe that makes a deal more attractive.

entries.clue: Go for Glaswegian group committing crimes? (4)

blocks.note: the Scots verb for go, as a Glaswegian would say it

annotation.surface: A suggestion to join a Glasgow crime gang.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For Glaswegian' flags a Scots word, and the crime group supplies the same letters as a straight noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use and a plain synonym: the Scots verb as in 'gang aft agley', and the ordinary noun for a criminal band.

entries.clue: Offer Cambridge University loan previously (6)

indicatorNotes.previously: previously means earlier, so the loan comes first, before the university

blocks.note: a sub is a small advance or loan
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, in Cambridge, Massachusetts

annotation.surface: A student is offered a loan by Cambridge University in advance.
annotation.walkthrough: Cambridge University suggests the English one; it is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. A sub is British slang for an advance on wages.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you put forward a proposal or an entry for someone else to consider.

entries.clue: Those queuing for free food rebel, and I worried (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition names the people; the answer is the queue they form
annotation.surface: Someone in a food queue frets alongside a rebel.
annotation.walkthrough: The punctuation splits 'rebel' from 'and I', but both belong in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A breadline is a queue of people waiting for free food handed out by charity.

entries.clue: Historian, one breaking down on the radio (8)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: radio is heard, not seen, so the answer only has to sound like the phrase

blocks.note: an analyst breaks things down into parts

annotation.surface: A historian breaks down in tears during a radio interview.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breaking down' suggests collapse; it means analysing. 'One' supplies the article: 'an analyst' said quickly.
annotation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, year-by-year records, so is a historian.

entries.clue: Hors d’oeuvres and beer consumed by social worker, quietly downing two litres (9)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: IPA is swallowed by the letters around it
indicatorNotes.downing: STILL drinks down, and so loses, the two Ls

blocks.note: ants are social insects and workers
STILL = quietly, minus L and L

annotation.surface: Starters and beer are knocked back by a social worker who quietly downs two litres.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is the crossword's ant, and 'quietly' is the fodder STILL rather than P; 'downing' means drinking up its two Ls.
annotation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian starters, the equivalent of hors d'oeuvres.

entries.clue: Husband enters New Year drunk in whatever location (8)

indicatorNotes.enters: H goes into the mixed letters

annotation.surface: A husband staggers in drunk at New Year, anywhere at all.
annotation.walkthrough: New Year and drunk fit the party scene; 'New Year' is the fodder, and the H sits inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Anywhere means in any place at all, whatever the location.

entries.clue: Type of table sauce (8)

blocks.note: the bedroom table with a mirror, where you get ready
the oil-and-vinegar kind poured over salad

annotation.surface: A question of which sauce belongs on the dining table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Table sauce' reads as one thing, like ketchup; split it, and each half is its own definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The first is completed by the answer as a compound noun; the second is a plain synonym for a salad sauce.

entries.clue: Emotion drained, male is in gloomy state (7)

indicatorNotes.drained: EMOTION emptied of its contents leaves EN
indicatorNotes.in: 'is in' places one thing inside another, so EN and M sit within DARK

annotation.surface: A man, emotionally exhausted, sinks into a gloomy state of mind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gloomy state' reads as a mood; 'state' alone is the definition, a nation, with a nod to Hamlet's 'something is rotten in the state of Denmark'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Scandinavian kingdom is one of many nations, and Hamlet calls it a state.

entries.clue: Those not scared about holding sparklers, maybe (6)

indicatorNotes.about: as in 'about turn', the letters face the other way and are read right to left
indicatorNotes.holding: the words hold the answer inside them

annotation.surface: People brave enough to hold lit sparklers on bonfire night.
annotation.walkthrough: The sparklers look like fireworks; they are gems, and 'maybe' warns that stones are only one kind of sparkler.
annotation.definitionFit: Precious stones sparkle, so they are sparklers by example.

entries.clue: Jerk working as ship’s doctor (7)

blocks.note: a jerk is a sudden surge
a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: An unpleasant man serving as the doctor on a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' reads as an insult; it is a sudden movement.
annotation.definitionFit: The doctor on a ship is traditionally called the ship's surgeon.

entries.clue: Flops down, perhaps exhausted after endless work mending pipes? (6)

indicatorNotes.after: PS comes after the other piece

blocks.note: to plumb is to do plumbing work; endless, it loses its B

annotation.surface: A plumber, worn out after a job fixing pipes, slumps down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps exhausted' reads like a guess at why someone flops down; it is PERHAPS with its inside drained.
annotation.definitionFit: To plump down is to drop heavily into a seat.

entries.clue: Knot bow tie at last (4)

indicatorNotes.at last: at last means at the end, so only the final letter of TIE is used

blocks.note: a bow of the head is a nod

annotation.surface: Finally knotting a bow tie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bow tie' looks like the neckwear; 'bow' is a nod of the head, and 'tie' only gives its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A node is a knot, as in a knotty swelling on a stem or joint.

entries.clue: Discovered idiot guards sick prisoner showing determination (9)

indicatorNotes.Discovered: uncovered: TWERP loses its outer letters
indicatorNotes.guards: a guard stands on either side of what it protects, so WER goes around ILL POW

blocks.note: TWERP without its cover letters T and P

annotation.surface: An exposed fool keeps watch over a sick inmate and shows resolve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found out; it means dis-covered, with the covering letters removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Willpower is determination, the strength to carry something through.

entries.clue: Place to find spare tyre lying unused reportedly (5)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the answer only has to sound right

annotation.surface: A spare tyre is lying unused somewhere in the boot.
annotation.walkthrough: The car's spare tyre is the natural reading; a spare tyre is also a roll of fat round the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A 'spare tyre' of fat sits around the waist.

entries.clue: Kitty ultimately raised for game (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately raised: in a down clue the last letter is lifted one place up

blocks.note: a kitty is a shared pool of money; its final L moves up past the second O

annotation.surface: The kitty is finally raised for a game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately raised' sounds like money finally collected; it moves the last letter of POOL up one place.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the horseback sport with mallets is one of countless games.

entries.clue: “Fatty” Arbuckle, originally flipping religious, shot bears (7)

indicatorNotes.flipping: to flip something is to turn it over, so PI is read backwards

blocks.note: a shot of medicine is a dose

annotation.surface: Silent-film comedian Roscoe 'Fatty' Arbuckle turns religious and shoots bears.
annotation.walkthrough: The nickname is lifted out as the definition. PI is the standard short form of pious.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from biology: the technical adjective for fat-storing, as in the tissue under the skin.

entries.clue: Popular service, wrong to be cut back (7)

indicatorNotes.back: EVI is turned back to IVE

blocks.note: EVIL, a wrong, with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A popular church service is wrongly scaled back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular' leads to IN or POP; here it is the definition, in the informal sense of a massive hit.
annotation.definitionFit: Informally, something massive is hugely successful or popular, as in a massive hit.

entries.clue: How to avoid a sunburnt back? Stay cool (4,4,5,2)

annotation.definition2: How to avoid a sunburnt back

blocks.clueFragment: How to avoid a sunburnt back
blocks.note: the literal reading: stay covered up

annotation.surface: Advice for a hot day: cover up to protect your back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stay cool' looks like advice about heat, matching the sunburn; it is the idiom for not losing your temper.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for not losing one's temper, paired with its literal sense of staying covered in the sun.
